Raw Client Material:

Discovery call notes, 6 October 2026 (fictional). Attendees: Dana Whitfield,
General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments (fictional); Ravi Okafor, CISO; Ingrid
Solberg, Head of Quality.

- Tamarack designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. HQ in
  the Netherlands; plants in the Netherlands and Germany; sales office in the
  United States. About 1,100 staff; Dana said revenue is "in the US$200 to
  300 million range".
- AI today: a customer service chatbot on the support portal is live
  (deployed). An AI visual inspection system on the German production line is
  in pilot. They plan to use AI for sales forecasting next year.
- Dana: "We are piloting, not scaling. I want governance in place before
  visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."
- Ravi: they run an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS; Ingrid runs the quality management
  system under ISO 9001. They would like to start ISO/IEC 42001 work next
  year.
- Dana named the EU AI Act and the GDPR as the rules they are watching.
- Internal audit reported in June 2026 that there is no inventory of AI
  systems.
- Constraints: budget approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year; customer
  data must stay in the EU; the German works council must be consulted before
  anything touches production staff.
- Who would attend: Dana, Ravi, Ingrid, the Head of Data (Tomas Reyes), the
  German plant manager and two internal auditors.
- Dana is the budget holder for this. Decision expected by 15 December 2026.

fail_indicators_seen: A field value not traceable to the raw material
A statement of a Client fact that Part 2 of the fixture (the Client Profile Block) does not contain, including any incumbent register, process, control or record beyond the framework names
judgment_calls: 'run by Ravi Okafor, CISO' is treated as an unsupported owner attribution. Ravi said 'they run' the ISMS, and another scorer could read it as a harmless gloss, since Ravi is the CISO and spoke for it.

'internal audit function' is treated as an incumbent function beyond the framework names. Another scorer could accept it because the template field mentions 'audit programs' and the material shows internal audit issued a June 2026 report. I did not see the fixture's Part 2 block and inferred its content from the guidance.
The 'presumed to mean 2027' reading of 'next year' is flagged in CONFIDENCE_NOTES and not asserted as a fact in a field, so I did not count it as a failure.
Placing the Q2 2027 timeline under STATED_CONSTRAINTS, taken from Dana's objective, is treated as restatement and not as a new fact.
score.reasoning: The format, completeness and halt checks are met. Checklist item 3 and the corresponding fail indicators are not. The INCUMBENT_FRAMEWORKS field attributes ownership of the ISMS to Ravi Okafor, which the material does not state. It also lists an 'internal audit function' as an incumbent program. The material supports only an audit report and the attendance of two internal auditors, and the response's own CONFIDENCE_NOTES say the function's scope and program are not described. Under v1.14.3 guidance, owner attributions and incumbent functions not in the Profile Block are failures, and a case passes only if every element is met. The verdict is FAIL.
